page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of system memory. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, featuring 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU allocation is dedicated, and the processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU execution, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25% of evaluated systems. However, multi-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the average range. A notable bottleneck is observed in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, which registers in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is consistently average, measuring 45.33 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 26.94 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Static web serving throughput reaches an average of 8.25 GB/sec, while LLM inference for a small 135M model achieves 486.13 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 190.13 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-standard-8 offers a balanced resource density of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU, making it a viable option for workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The primary tradeoff is the lack of local NVMe storage and hardware acceleration, which limits its utility for high-speed database logging or heavy machine learning training. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, software compilation, text processing, and moderate database operations.
